bug_description.normalized: The staged 24604-byte witness starts with bytes `0x20 0xff`, so `spng_read_fuzzer_structure_aware` selects stream mode (`stream = 1`) and passes the remaining 24602 bytes through `spng_set_png_stream()`. `spng_decoded_image_size()` calls `get_ancillary()` before checking the invalid `fmt = 127`, so libspng parses pre-IDAT chunks anyway. In the saved PNG stream, the chunk header at byte offset 103 is `eXIf` with declared length 8224. `read_header()` parses that header into its local `chunk` and persists it in `ctx->current_chunk`; `read_chunks_before_idat()` then copies `ctx->current_chunk` into its own local `chunk`, keeps the chunk on the cached-read path, and snapshots `data = ctx->data` while `ctx->data` still points to the initial `SPNG_READ_SIZE` 8192-byte streaming buffer. `read_chunk_bytes()` then calls `read_data()` with `bytes = 8224`; the streaming path reallocates `ctx->data`, freeing the old buffer and installing a new 8224-byte one. The EXIF branch uses the copied local `chunk.type` and `chunk.length` and executes `memcpy(exif.data, data, chunk.length)` with local `data` still pointing at the freed buffer, producing the reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 8224` at `spng.c:1454`. The staged patch fixes this by moving `data = ctx->data` to after `read_chunk_bytes()`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled chunk metadata that drives the bug: the next pre-IDAT chunk header is parsed as length 8224 and type `eXIf`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` begins with harness bytes `0x20 0xff`, so the fuzzer strips them, selects `spng_set_png_stream()`, and streams the remaining 24602 bytes as PNG data. After IHDR and four private `0x20202020` chunks, the next 8 PNG bytes at offset 103 are `00 00 20 20 65 58 49 66`, which parse here as `chunk.length = 8224` and `chunk.type = eXIf`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The EXIF handler copies 8224 bytes from local `data`, but that pointer still aliases the old 8192-byte stream buffer that `read_data()` just freed via `realloc()`.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `heap-use-after-free READ of size 8224` at `spng.c:1454` with the free at `read_data:292` and the allocation at `spng_set_png_stream:2382`.

root_cause.description: The function snapshots `ctx->data` into local `data` before `read_chunk_bytes(ctx, chunk.length)`, even though the streaming read path can `realloc(ctx->data, chunk.length)` and free the aliased buffer. The fix moves this assignment after `read_chunk_bytes()` so `data` is refreshed from the post-reallocation pointer.
root_cause.note: The staged patch's only logic change on this path is deleting line 1049 before the read and re-inserting `data = ctx->data;` immediately after the `read_chunk_bytes()` call.

tainted_value_origin.description: This header parse produces the exact attacker-controlled values later stored in `ctx->current_chunk` and copied into `read_chunks_before_idat()`'s local `chunk`: `chunk.length = 8224`, which exceeds the current 8192-byte stream buffer and forces reallocation, and `chunk.type = eXIf`, which selects the EXIF copy sink.

parser_admitted.description: Even though the witness uses `fmt = 127`, `spng_decoded_image_size()` first calls `get_ancillary(ctx)`. The streamed PNG therefore reaches `read_chunks_before_idat()` before the later `fmt` check at line 2477 could return `SPNG_EFMT`.

coarse_trace.summary: The structure-aware harness interprets the first two witness bytes, takes the stream path because `data[1] >> 7 == 1`, and calls `spng_set_png_stream()` before `spng_decoded_image_size()`.
libspng allocates the initial `SPNG_READ_SIZE` 8192-byte streaming buffer in `ctx->data`, records the read callback, and marks the context as streaming.

While parsing pre-IDAT chunks, libspng materializes the current chunk header as `eXIf` with length 8224, stores it in `ctx->current_chunk`, copies it into the loop-local `chunk`, admits it to the cached-read path, and snapshots `data = ctx->data` before reading the body.

Because the streamed EXIF body length 8224 exceeds the current `ctx->data_size` 8192, `read_data()` grows `ctx->data` with `realloc()`, freeing the aliased old buffer and leaving local `data` dangling.
The EXIF handler allocates `exif.data` and then `memcpy`s 8224 bytes from the stale local alias, triggering the reproduced ASan heap-use-after-free read.

fine_trace.note: Because the witness's second harness byte is `0xff`, the fuzzer takes the stream path and calls `spng_set_png_stream()`. libspng allocates the initial `SPNG_READ_SIZE` buffer, sets `ctx->data_size = 8192`, records the read callback, and marks `ctx->streaming = 1`. ASan's allocation stack attributes the later freed region to this allocation site.

Source. After `read_data(ctx, 8)` has loaded the next chunk header from the stream into `ctx->data`, these statements materialize the current pre-IDAT chunk as length 8224 and type `eXIf`. In the saved witness this header begins at PNG offset 103, after IHDR and four private `0x20202020` chunks.

The parsed header from step 2 is persisted into `ctx->current_chunk`. Later logic does not keep using `read_header()`'s local `chunk`; the cache check consults `ctx->current_chunk`, and the loop body copies this persisted state into its own local `chunk`.

At the top of the loop body, `read_chunks_before_idat()` copies the persisted header into its own local `chunk`. This copied `chunk` is the source-level object later used by the IDAT check, `read_chunk_bytes(ctx, chunk.length)`, and the EXIF dispatch.

The cache-admission check uses `ctx->current_chunk.length = 8224` and succeeds under the harness-set limits `max_chunk_size = 4000000` and `chunk_cache_limit = 8000000`, so the discard branch is skipped and execution reaches the body read for this same copied chunk.

Root cause. After cache admission and before reading the chunk body, the function snapshots the current buffer pointer into local `data`. At this point `data` and `ctx->data` still alias the original 8192-byte stream buffer from step 1.

During `read_chunk_bytes(ctx, chunk.length)`, the copied `chunk.length = 8224` becomes `bytes = 8224`. Because `ctx->data_size = 8192`, `spng__realloc` grows `ctx->data` to 8224 bytes. ASan reports this `realloc` as the free site: the old 8192-byte buffer that local `data` still aliases is freed, and `ctx->data` now points to the new allocation.

Post-read state after read_chunk_bytes returns successfully. The local data pointer still holds the old buffer captured in step 6, while the nested realloc in step 7 has replaced ctx->data. This is the verified stale-alias state that propagates to the later EXIF copy.

depends_on.via: data retains the pre-read ctx->data value

fine_trace.note: After the body read, the copied local `chunk.type` still matches `type_exif`, so execution enters the EXIF handler for this 8224-byte chunk instead of falling through to another handler.

Sink. The EXIF path allocates `exif.data` to `chunk.length` bytes, but this `memcpy` still reads from local `data` captured in step 6 rather than from the reallocated `ctx->data`. With the copied `chunk.length = 8224`, the copy reads from the freed 8192-byte region and ASan reports `heap-use-after-free READ of size 8224` here.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch deletes the pre-read `data = ctx->data;` and reassigns `data` only after `read_chunk_bytes()`, so the EXIF copy uses the post-`realloc` buffer instead of a freed alias. Stage 02 did not run the fixed image; this is a source-level conclusion from `patch.diff`.

format.name: libspng structure-aware fuzzer input
format.contract: Exactly the staged witness shape: first byte `0x20`, second byte `0xff` so the harness uses `stream = 1` and `fmt = 127`, followed by a PNG byte stream whose pre-IDAT chunk list reaches an `eXIf` header at PNG offset 103 with declared length 8224 after four private `0x20202020` chunks. That exact combination makes `read_chunks_before_idat()` cache the original 8192-byte `ctx->data`, `read_chunk_bytes()` grow it with `realloc()`, and the EXIF branch immediately `memcpy()` from the stale alias.
